title: Quantifying the global binding and target-search dynamics of epigenetic regulatory factors using live-cell single-molecule tracking
protocol: Seed HEK293T cells the day before transfection such that a 100 × 20 mm dish reaches 90% confluency (∼ 3 × 10^6 cells) in 14 mL of complete HEK293T cell medium the following day.
Prepare Solution A for transfection mixture using CaPO4 as directed.
Add accurately measured volumes of psPAX-2, pMD2.G, and the gene of interest plasmids to the transfection mixture.
Adjust pH of 2× HBSS to 7.1 by dropwise adding 10 N NaOH.
Filter-sterilize the adjusted 2× HBSS through a 0.22 μm filter flask.
Ensure all material in contact with virus is treated with detergent and sterilized by UV light before autoclaving for final sterilization.
Add 1,050 μL of 2 × HBSS dropwise while vortexing to reach halfway up the side of a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Wait at least 5 seconds between drops so that the addition takes around 3–5 minutes.
Vortex the solution at maximum speed for 1.5 minutes to ensure proper mixing.
Incubate the mixture between 20°C and 25°C until marginal turbidity is observed, typically around 10 minutes.
Plate the transfection mixture dropwise evenly over the entire plate of cells.
Break the plate into thirds and plate a 700 μL volume per section to ensure an even distribution.
Incubate at 37°C in 5% CO2 for 12 hours.
Store cells within a separate tray or container inside the incubator.
Incubate cells.
Observe cells under a light microscope.
Look for cell fusion to form large colonies and cell bursting.
Note if more than 10% of cells have changed, reduce initial incubation time accordingly.
Remove medium into a separate container with detergent added (1.5–2.0% LpH®se Nonsterile Disinfectant).
Place used pipettes in the detergent-containing solution to neutralize virus.
Fill plate with fresh HEK293T culture medium and incubate for 5 minutes at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Repeat steps of removing medium and treating pipettes with detergent one more time.
Add 12 mL of fresh HEK293T culture medium to the cells.
Ensure all virus-containing medium and equipment is treated with detergent and UV-sterilized before autoclaving for sterilization.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 48 h.
Harvest viral titer from HEK293T cells.
Infect mES cells with the gene of interest using lentivirus and polybrene.
Select cells integrated with the gene of interest using puromycin.
Create a single-cell suspension of mES cells by transferring 20% of an 80% confluent dish.
Centrifuge to pellet cells at 300 rcf for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove medium and resuspend cells in 1.0 mL of 5 × mES culture medium.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 50 mL falcon tube.
Collect virus-containing medium from HEK293T cells.
Centrifuge the medium at 1,000 rcf for 5 minutes at 4°C to remove dead cells.
Transfer the virus-containing medium to a falcon tube containing mES cells.
Add polybrene to achieve a final concentration of 8 μg/mL.
Incubate the solution at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 6–8 hours, resuspending every 2 hours.
Plate the entire solution onto a gelatinated 100 × 20 mm dish.
Incubate the cells at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 12 hours.
Remove the medium by pipetting into a separate container containing detergent.
Replace the medium with 10 mL of mES medium.
Repeat the process every day until cells reach 60% confluency.
Add 2.0 μg/mL puromycin for selection when replacing medium.
Remove medium via suction once cells have been split and transferred to a culture dish.
Maintain cells in the presence of puromycin for at least one week.
Reduce puromycin concentration to 1.0 μg/mL after initial selection period.
Freeze cells in liquid nitrogen for later use to preserve cell lines.
Split mES cells every 2–3 days with daily medium changes to prevent differentiation.
Culture cells in the absence or presence of 0.1 ug/mL doxycycline for 72 hours.
Coat the bottom of imaging plates with 0.2% gelatin.
Remove gelatin and replace with fresh gelatin after 12-16 hours.
Seed cells into imaging plates with 0.5–0.7 million cells per plate in a single-cell suspension to form a monolayer.
Incubate the seeded cells at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 16-24 hours.
Remove culture media and add fresh media containing 50 pM JF549 HaloTag® dye.
Incubate for 15 min at 37°C with 5% CO2 covered from light.
Remove the culture media by pipetting and discard it.
Gently wash the cells once with PBS.
Add fresh culture medium and incubate for 30 min at 37°C with 5% CO2 covered from light.
Remove the culture media by pipetting and discard it.
Gently wash the cells once with PBS.
Add FluoroBrite DMEM live-cell imaging medium supplemented with 10% FBS into the imaging plate.

Acquire images using an Axio Observer D1 (Zeiss, Germany) Total Internal Reflection (TIRF) microscope equipped with an Alpha Plan-apochromat 100 × /1.46 oil immersion objective (Zeiss, Germany) with an additional 2.5 × magnification on the emission pathway.
Maintain cells at 37°C using a single-channel temperature controller (TC-324, Warner Instruments).
Acquire all images within 90 min from taking cells out of 5% CO2.
Focus on a single nucleus such that as many particles as possible are clear.
Stably bound proteins are easier to identify and so the eye is drawn to them.
Ensure transiently bound particles are still visible.
Take a stroboscopic video of the nuclei with intensification 200–700, number of frames 100, dark time (ms) 0 or 20, exposure time (ms) 30 or 10, laser power (mW) 7.5, TIRF angle 6.65–6.80.
Adjust the TIRF angle and focus as needed between each cell imaged due to depth and curvature changes.

Cells cultured in 0.1 μg/mL doxycycline for 3 days were treated with JF549 dye at picomolar concentration level to label only a subset of molecules (between 5–20 for any given frame) for accurate tracking of individual molecules.
Limit the number of molecules per frame because crossing tracks are difficult for algorithms to account for.
This data is used to obtain the residence time of bound protein and fraction of specific and non-specific interactions.
Coat the bottom of the imaging plate with 0.2% gelatin.
Remove the gelatin and replace it with fresh gelatin after 12–16 h.
Seed cells into multiple imaging plates as a single-cell suspension in one layer.
Incubate the cells at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 16 to 24 hours.
Remove the culture media by pipetting.
Add fresh culture media containing 10–50 pM JF549 HaloTag® Ligand.
Incubate for 15 minutes at 37°C with 5% CO2 covered from light.
Remove the culture media by pipetting and discard it.
Gently wash the cells once with PBS.
Add fresh culture medium and incubate for 30 minutes at 37°C with 5% CO2 covered from light.
Remove the culture media by pipetting and discard it.
Gently wash the cells once with PBS.
Add FluoroBrite DMEM live-cell imaging medium supplemented with 10% FBS into the imaging plate.

Acquire images using an Axio Observer D1 (Zeiss, Germany) Total Internal Reflection (TIRF) microscope equipped with an Alpha Plan-apochromat 100 × /1.46 oil immersion objective and additional 2.5 × magnification on the emission pathway.
Use a Solid-state Laser-stack (3i) to excite Janelia Fluor® 549 HaloTag® Ligand at 552 nm.
Apply a Brightline® single-band laser filter set for the excitation and emission spectra of JF549 and HaloTag® TMR ligand.
Maintain cells at 37°C using a single-channel temperature controller (TC-324, Warner Instruments).
Acquire all images within 90 min from taking cells out of 5% CO2.
Focus on a single nucleus to ensure as many particles are clear and stably bound proteins are visible.
Take a stroboscopic video of the nuclei under conditions of intensification 500–700, number of frames 400, dark time (ms) 170, exposure time (ms) 30, laser power (mW) 2.25, and TIRF angle 6.65–6.80.
Ensure cells are healthy and securely attached to the surface of the coverslip before imaging to avoid false movement during video acquisition.
Adjust TIRF angle and focus between each cell imaged.
Ensure intensification adjustments for clear final images after export.
Use HaloTag® TMR Ligand at 20–50 nM concentration to stain condensates.
Utilize Janelia Fluor® 646 (JF646) dye at picomolar concentration to track molecules within condensates.
Take initial images of condensates.
Capture time lapse of molecular dynamics immediately after initial imaging.
Acquire another image of condensates to check for cell movement during acquisition.
Coat the bottom of the imaging plate with 0.2% gelatin the day before splitting cells for imaging.
Remove and replace gelatin with fresh solution after 12–16 h.
Seed cells into the imaging plates after removing gelatin.
Seed the cells into multiple imaging plates in a single-cell suspension as one layer.
Incubate the cells at 37°C with 5% CO2 overnight.
Remove the culture media by pipetting.
Add fresh culture media with 300 pM JF646 for 15 min at 37°C away from light.
Remove the culture media by pipetting.
Add fresh culture media supplemented with 20 nM HaloTag® TMR Ligand and incubate for 15 min at 37°C with 5% CO2 covered from light.
Remove the culture media by pipetting and discard it.
Gently wash the cells once with PBS.
Add fresh culture medium and incubate for 60 min at 37°C with 5% CO2 covered from light.
Remove the culture media by pipetting and discard it.
Gently wash the cells once with PBS.
Add FluoroBrite DMEM live-cell imaging medium supplemented with 10% FBS into the imaging plate.
Maintain cells at 37°C using a single-channel temperature controller.
Acquire images within 90 min of removing cells from 5% CO2 environment.
Use an Axio Observer D1 Total Internal Reflection (TIRF) microscope with Alpha Plan-apochromat 100 × /1.46 oil immersion objective.
Visualize TMR ligand-bound proteins using a Brightline single-band laser filter set for excitation, emission and dichroic mirror.
Visualize HaloTag JF646-labeled proteins using another Brightline single-band laser filter set for excitation, emission and dichroic mirror.
Focus on a single nucleus to ensure clarity of as many particles as possible.
Take an image to determine the distribution of HT-bound proteins by exciting HaloTag TMR.

Capture a video of the nucleus using HaloTag JF646 with specified conditions: intensification 300, number of frames 50, dark time 0 ms, exposure time 30 ms, laser power 30 mW, and TIRF angle between 6.65–6.80 degrees.
Adjust TIRF angle and focus as needed between cells due to differences in depth and curvature.
Take an image of HaloTag® TMR to ensure there is no shifting of the cell during video acquisition.
